input: Learn to hand-letter envelopes for wedding stationery

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Hand-lettering covers a wide range — from basic print styles to brush calligraphy to pointed-pen calligraphy. Knowing which style(s) to focus on completely changes the tools, tutorials, and practice path.
Whether the wedding is in 6 weeks or 12 months determines how intensive the learning schedule needs to be and whether a beginner can realistically self-teach or should hire help.
Knowing the volume — how many envelopes need to be addressed — affects how much practice is required to achieve consistency and whether the skill needs to be production-level or just presentable.
Whether this is for the user's own wedding, a friend's, or a side business changes the stakes, the style expectations, and the level of perfection required.
The user may have zero supplies or already own some materials. Knowing their starting point avoids redundant advice and helps identify the exact next purchase or action.

Wedding aesthetics vary hugely — modern minimalist, romantic script, vintage copperplate, etc. The target style determines which specific lettering technique to learn and which reference materials to use.

The user's definition of 'done well' could range from 'legible and pretty' to 'professional calligrapher quality.' This sets the bar for how much practice is needed and whether self-teaching is sufficient.

gold.taskTitle: Learn hand-lettering for wedding envelope addressing
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to develop hand-lettering skills specifically for addressing envelopes for wedding stationery.

questions.title: Which lettering style are you aiming to learn?
questions.description: Is the goal brush calligraphy (e.g., with a brush pen), pointed-pen calligraphy (e.g., copperplate/Spencerian), or a modern hand-lettered print style? The style determines tools, techniques, and tutorials entirely.

questions.title: How much time do you have before the envelopes are needed?
questions.description: What is the deadline — weeks or months away? This determines how intensive the practice schedule needs to be and whether self-teaching is realistic in the available time.

questions.title: Roughly how many envelopes need to be addressed?
questions.description: Is this 30 envelopes or 300? Volume affects how much consistency and stamina need to be built, and how much practice is needed before tackling the real stationery.

questions.title: Is this for your own wedding or someone else's?
questions.description: Are you the bride/groom, a friend helping out, or building a skill for a side business? This shapes the pressure level, style freedom, and how polished the final result needs to be.

questions.title: What supplies do you already have on hand?
questions.description: Do you own any brush pens, dip pens, nibs, ink, or practice paper, or are you starting from scratch? This determines whether the immediate next step is buying materials or beginning practice.

questions.title: What aesthetic or visual style are you going for?
questions.description: Is the wedding vibe romantic and flowing, sleek and modern, vintage, bohemian? Having a target aesthetic — ideally with a reference image — makes it possible to choose the right letterforms to study.

questions.title: What does a successful result look like to you?
questions.description: Are you aiming for 'charming and handmade' or 'indistinguishable from a professional calligrapher'? Your quality bar determines how many weeks of practice to plan for and whether a trial run on spare envelopes is needed.
